properties.name: Redwood National and State Parks
properties.description: Old-growth redwoods here have been targeted by illegal logging and burl poaching, where sections are cut from living trees to sell as wood carvings.

properties.name: Olympic National Park
properties.description: Protected old-growth cedar and bigleaf maple have been targeted by timber poaching, with trees felled inside park and adjacent forest boundaries and sold on the black market.

properties.name: Death Valley National Park
properties.description: A long mining history left many abandoned claims. The park continues to deal with unauthorized digging and disturbance at legacy mineral sites.

properties.name: Mojave National Preserve
properties.description: The preserve contains many old mining claims and sees unauthorized mineral prospecting and disturbance across its desert lands.

properties.name: Sequoia and Kings Canyon National Parks
properties.description: Remote groves have been cleared for illegal cannabis cultivation, which damages forest, diverts streams, and leaves behind chemicals and waste.

properties.name: Wrangell-St. Elias National Park and Preserve
properties.description: This park surrounds historic mining districts such as Kennecott. Active and abandoned claims create ongoing pressure from unauthorized mineral extraction.

properties.name: Great Smoky Mountains National Park
properties.description: Beyond wildlife poaching, the park faces illegal harvesting of forest products such as ginseng and galax, removing protected plants for sale.
